subject: Pacific Health — evidence of backup deletion and log retention exception
messages:
From: Linda Cho <linda.cho@pacifichealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>, audit@pacifichealth.com
Date: Wed, 26 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Evidence request: backups & logs deletion cadence

Hi Kimberly —

Quick one: Pacific Health is working through an upcoming regulator audit (state health records) and they asked us to provide confirmation and evidence that (1) cold backup snapshots older than 90 days are purged on schedule and (2) application access logs are subject to a 180-day deletion policy unless a documented forensic exception exists.

Two asks from the audit team: a) a short statement we can include in the audit package confirming the purge cadence and where the evidence (snapshots + deletion runbook) lives, and b) the list of subprocessors involved in storing backups/logs with the retention windows you apply to each.

We need something by next Tuesday (Dec 2) to include in the package. If you need a signed addendum to the DPA to cover a temporary extension for a narrow set of logs for our investigation team, let us know and we can route it through legal.

Thanks —
Linda
Linda Cho
Senior IT Auditor
Pacific Health

Attachment: audit_request_form.pdf (stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Nov 2025 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: backups & logs deletion cadence

Hi Linda — thanks for the clear ask and deadline. We'll self-attest the standard retention/erase schedules and bundle the runbook evidence. Quick notes: 

- Snapshot purge: our standard is automated snapshot pruning at 90 days for cold backups; we keep immutable daily snapshots for 30 days and weekly snapshots beyond that until the 90-day purge window. I will include the purge logs and snapshot manifest for October/November.
- Application access logs: default retention 180 days; for investigations we can request a temporary retention hold for a scoped set of log keys (forensic ticket required).
- Subprocessors: we maintain a subprocessor matrix; the backup object store is managed by StorageCo under a subcontract (bucket: redwood-pac-backups), and archival copies are replicated to a third-party escrow provider for legal escrow (controlled by our ops).

I will assemble a one-page statement for your package and attach the runbook and subprocessor list. If Pacific needs a DPA addendum for a temporary, documented exception, we can draft an addendum and route to DocuSign — please confirm who in your legal team should sign.

Next steps: Karthik, can you pull the purge manifest and the bucket ACL/KMS key IDs for the storageco buckets so we can include proof-of-delete entries? Marissa, I'll need the DPA addendum template if we go that route.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Linda Cho <linda.cho@pacifichealth.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Nov 2025 15:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: backups & logs deletion cadence

Kimberly / Linda — attaching a short technical summary below (will put full manifests on the shared Drive link):

- Storage topology: backups live in StorageCo S3-compatible buckets (redwood-pac-backups) in us-west-2 and are encrypted with CMKs in our AWS account. Weekly snapshots are retained for 90 days; lifecycle policy transitions older snapshots to cold storage and then delete at purge.
- Proof-of-delete: StorageCo produces a deletion manifest when lifecycle deletes objects; we run a verify job that captures object tombstone entries into our audit index (immutable). I can export the verify job output for Oct 1–Nov 30 (file: verify_delete_manifest_202510-11.csv).
- Logs: application access logs (prod) are written to a separate LZ log bucket with 180-day lifecycle. Forensic holds are scoped by ticket and applied to object prefixes; we record holds in the ticket and retention-control index.
- Subprocessor contact for manifests: archive_ops@storageco.example — I copied them below to request confirmation of manifest exports.

I will upload: verify_delete_manifest_202510-11.csv and a small script log showing the tombstone entries.

1) DPA addendum: if Pacific requests a temporary retention extension for specific logs, we'll need a narrow-scope addendum (timebox + key prefixes + ticketing SLA) and an authorized signer on their side. Kimberly, I pushed a draft addendum to the Drive: dpa_addendum_draft.docx (link below).
2) Evidence artifacts: please include the following in the audit bundle:
   - purge_manifest.csv (verify_delete_manifest_202510-11.csv from Karthik)
   - snapshot_manifest_oct_nov.json (metadata only)
   - subprocessor_matrix.csv (current version attached)
   - runbook excerpt (backup_purge_runbook_v1.pdf) showing the automation job and retention policy
3) Vendor confirmation: I'll loop StorageCo procurement for a signed confirmation of the deletion manifests. archive_ops@storageco.example — can you confirm you'll provide signed manifests for the last 90 days and the KMS key IDs used to encrypt the snapshot objects?
